title: GitHub Actions cache-mode policy (.github/policy.rego): workflows default to top-level cache-mode none, and jobs grant read or write
answers: Why does my new workflow fail the policy check with 'Missing cache-mode'?
How do I give one job in a workflow access to the Actions cache?
Why is cache-mode: none rejected on a job in a workflow file?
Where is the default cache access for CI workflows set and enforced?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_top_level_cache_mode and deny_redundant_job_cache_mode check every workflow file (files with `jobs`; composite actions are skipped) for the cache access level that GitHub Actions grants the run, which controls whether caches can be restored or saved.
Rule: Each workflow sets top-level `cache-mode: none`, then grants `cache-mode: read` (restore only) or `cache-mode: write` (populates a cache) on the specific job that needs it. A top-level value other than `none` is denied, and a job-level `cache-mode: none` is denied as redundant because job values override the workflow value and omitting the key already inherits the default.
Constraints: Job-level values take precedence over the workflow-level value for that job only, so grants never leak to sibling jobs. Newly added workflows need the top-level line or Conftest reports the missing-key message. Composite actions are not checked by these rules.
applies: Workflow YAML under .github/workflows; checked by Conftest with .github/policy.rego. Does not cover composite action.yml files or non-cache permissions.
says: A new continuous integration pipeline fails policy checks because cache mode is missing.
Build pipeline checks fail when individual jobs redundantly specify disabled caching access.
Grant read or write build cache access to a specific continuous integration job.
Ensure automated testing pipelines disable build caching by default to avoid cache leaks.
search: CI workflow cache policy in .github/policy.rego requires workflows with jobs to define top-level cache-mode: none, verified by deny_top_level_cache_mode and deny_redundant_job_cache_mode via Conftest. Specific jobs may grant cache-mode: read or cache-mode: write, while setting cache-mode: none at job level is rejected as redundant. This rule applies to workflow YAML files under .github/workflows and does not inspect composite action.yml files.
